proof:
# A genuine critical six-fiber chain crosses the empty-residual region
sufficient transit invariant in
`candidate 978c08161183f331`.
It is NOT an OC counterexample and does NOT violate its original KKT row.
The positive boundary term is exactly compensated, as calculated below.

## 1. Actual body and the all-halfspace assertion

Let T be a triangle of area one, g its centroid, and put

    C=[-2,3] times T,
    S={-2,-1,0,1,2,3} times T,
    gamma=4/9, c=sqrt(5)/3.

All fibers have area one; M=6 and max V=1<M/2. The global maximum raw
mixed depth is EXACTLY

    Q=2+gamma=22/9,                                     (1)

and the only deepest points are (0,g) and (1,g). The all-ambient-halfspace
lower bound needed for this claim is proved in Sections2--3, using a
finite exact polynomial nonnegativity certificate. No direction screen
or numerical optimization is used in that proof.

For an upper bound valid at any point x of an interior fiber, write
lambda_0,lambda_1,lambda_2 for the barycentric coordinates of T. Some
lambda_i(x)>=1/3. The own cap lambda_i>=lambda_i(x) has area
(1-lambda_i(x))^2<=4/9. A sufficiently large integer tilt isolates this
own cap together with all fibers on a chosen side, excluding the other
side. At bases0,1 choose the side with two fibers, giving at most22/9.
At bases-1,2 the analogous bound is13/9, and at the extreme bases it is4/9.
If x!=g at base0 or1, its maximal barycentric coordinate is strictly
greater than1/3, so this upper bound is strictly smaller than22/9.
Thus the lower bound at (0,g), and its reflected counterpart at(1,g),
prove both(1) and the complete deepest-point assertion.

## 2. Reduction of EVERY ambient normal to an explicit two-parameter function

Every containing closed halfspace can be moved inward to pass through
(0,g). A purely integer normal then captures at least three entire
fibers, giving mass at least3>22/9; its boundary fiber is included.
For a nonzero continuous normal, translate its scalar projection so
the centroid has value0 and divide by minus its lowest vertex value.
After ordering the three vertices, the normalized projected values are

    -1, t, 1-t,                  -1<=t<=1/2.

Their sum is zero because the triangle centroid is their average.
For -1<t<1/2, the fraction of the triangle above threshold s is

    F_t(s)=1                                      if s<=-1,
           1-(s+1)^2/[(t+1)(2-t)]                 if -1<=s<=t,
           (1-t-s)^2/[(2-t)(1-2t)]                if t<=s<=1-t,
           0                                      if s>=1-t.       (2)

The lower and upper quadratic expressions follow by computing the
similar corner triangle cut off at the lower or upper projected vertex.
They agree at the middle vertex threshold. The cases t=-1 and t=1/2
are their continuous limits, equivalently direct triangular cone cuts.
Nonzero continuous normals give boundary sets of area zero in every
fiber, so closed halfspaces cause no discrepancy in(2).

The total through-(0,g) mass therefore equals

    G(t,L)=sum_(k=-2)^3 F_t(k L),                         (3)

where L is the normalized integer coefficient, with either sign allowed.
It suffices to consider L>=0: changing negative L to |L| leaves the five
terms k=-2,...,2 unchanged as a group, and replaces F_t(-3|L|) by the
no-larger value F_t(3|L|). Thus G(t,L)>=G(t,|L|).

If L>=2, both negative-base fibers are fully captured and all positive-
base fibers contribute zero. Hence G=2+F_t(0)>=22/9. For t<=0 the last
inequality follows directly from

    9(1-t)^2-4(2-t)(1-2t)=(t+1)^2>=0;

for t>=0, F_t(0)=1-1/[(1+t)(2-t)]>=1/2>4/9.
It remains to prove

    G(t,L)>=22/9 on [-1,1/2] times [0,2].                (4)

## 3. An explicit exact nonnegativity certificate for(4)

Here all coefficients and all polygon vertices are rational. The complete
certificate is `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/triangle-six-fiber-depth-bernstein-certificate.json`;
AppendixA below prints its polygon subdivision and all Bernstein
coefficients as ordinary rational data, so it is not necessary to trust
an optimization routine or a floating-point calculation.

Partition the rectangle by the threshold lines

    k L=-1, k L=t, k L=1-t  (k=-2,-1,1,2,3), and t=0.

Lines not meeting the rectangle have no effect. The resulting22 convex
polygon cells have constant choices of the four branches in(2). Define

    D(t)=(t+1)(2-t)(1-2t),
    P(t,L)=9 D(t)[G(t,L)-22/9].                         (5)

On each cell P is a polynomial of degree at most3. For example, a full
term contributes9D, a zero term contributes0, a lower quadratic term
contributes9[D-(kL+1)^2(1-2t)], and an upper quadratic term contributes
9(1-t-kL)^2(t+1). The constant subtraction contributes-22D.
These rules unambiguously determine the polynomial independently of
the certificate's stored coefficients.

The certificate triangulates the22 cells into38 rational triangles.
For a triangle with ordered vertices A,B,C, substitute
(t,L)=A+u(B-A)+v(C-A), where u,v>=0 and u+v<=1. If the transformed
polynomial is sum_(a+b<=3) p_ab u^a v^b, its degree3 triangular Bernstein
coefficient indexed by i,j>=0, i+j<=3 is

    b_ij=sum_(a<=i,b<=j) p_ab
          binom(i,a)binom(j,b)/[binom(3,a+b)binom(a+b,a)].          (6)

Indeed the degree3 basis is

    B_ij=3!/[i!j!(3-i-j)!] u^i v^j (1-u-v)^(3-i-j),

and the binomial identity expands every monomial u^a v^b as the weighted
sum prescribed by(6). Every B_ij is nonnegative on the triangle, so
nonnegative b_ij prove P>=0 there.

Every one of the380 coefficients listed in AppendixA is nonnegative.
The38 triangles cover the22 cells, and those cells cover the rectangle.
These coverage assertions can be checked exactly by the supplied polygon
vertices: triangles lie in their listed convex cells, have pairwise
intersections of area zero, and their areas sum to the cell area; the
cells likewise have pairwise intersections of area zero and total area3,
the area of the rectangle. A finite closed union contained in a rectangle
with these properties cannot omit a point of the rectangle: its relative
complement would be nonempty and relatively open, hence have positive
area. The same argument applies within each cell.

The independent verifier
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_triangle_six_depth_bernstein_certificate.py` uses ONLY integer
and Fraction arithmetic. It reconstructs every branch polynomial from(2),
checks that no listed cell crosses a branch boundary, independently
recomputes all380 coefficients by(6), and checks every coverage and
nonoverlap assertion by exact rational polygon intersections and areas.
It reports PASS for all22 cells and38 triangles. This is a verification
of the explicit algebraic certificate, not numerical evidence for(4).

In the open parameter strip -1<t<1/2, D(t)>0, so P>=0 proves(4).
The endpoint directions t=-1,1/2 follow by continuity of the area of a
halfspace cut of a triangle as its normal varies. The boundary hyperplane
has area zero, and dominated convergence gives that continuity, including
when its scalar threshold meets a projected vertex. This completes the
all-normal proof of(4), hence of the global depth claim(1).

## 4. Natural globally critical circuits and their exact original optimizer

Use the six original ambient caps, i=0,1,2,

    H_i={lambda_i(x)-2 z>=1/3},
    J_i={lambda_i(x)+2(z-1)>=1/3}.                       (7)

Every H_i captures the entire fibers at -2,-1, the canonical area4/9
cap at0, and zero area at1,2,3. Every J_i captures the entire fibers
at2,3, the canonical cap at1, and zero area at-2,-1,0. Each cap has
mass22/9, and by(1) is GENUINELY globally critical at its corresponding
deepest point. At0 the three H traces cover T, since some barycentric
coordinate is at least1/3; at1 the J traces cover T. The other fibers
are fully covered. These are actual local critical positive circuits,
not an artificial cover consisting of noncritical caps.

For the original one-cap residual program, the obstacle roots are

    e=(0,0,c,c,0,0),            c=sqrt(5)/3,             (8)

in base order -2,-1,0,1,2,3. The UNIQUE optimal sampled threshold is
h=(c,c,c,c,c,c). Indeed strict convexity gives a unique minimizer,
and reflection of the base preserves the program, so it is symmetric:
h=(a,b,v,v,b,a) with v>=c. Adjacent convexity implies a>=b>=v, hence
the objective is at least6c^2, achieved by the constant vector.

Let s=2c be the derivative at every site. In the nearest-neighbor KKT
realization, the multipliers are uniquely forced to be

    beta/s=(0,1,3,3,1,0),
    lambda/s=(0,0,3,3,0,0).                             (9)

The outer four obstacle inequalities have strict slack, so their
lambda values vanish. The endpoint stationarity equations force the
adjacent beta to equal s; the next equations force the two central
beta values to equal3s. The two remaining stationarity equations give
lambda=3s at each center. All second-difference constraints are tight,
so these are valid original KKT data with zero supporting slopes.

For any H_i chosen at source0, the actual residual roots are

    f=(0,0,c,1,1,1).                                    (10)

The positive-beta component J={-1,0,1,2} includes base-1, whose strict
residual is EMPTY. It therefore crosses the empty-residual region,
even though the source cap is globally critical and has own fraction
exactly gamma_2. The condition that the positive-beta component remain
inside the nonempty residual interval is consequently NOT automatic,
even for this natural critical-circuit cover and the uniquely determined
nearest-neighbor KKT multipliers.

## 5. The original row remains good by exact boundary compensation

Solving the four-state tridiagonal Green equations, or directly multiplying
the original finite absorbing-chain matrix, gives the normalized terminal
row from source0:

    theta=(2,2,2,1,1,1)/9.                              (11)

Its barycenter is0. The Green coefficients at bases -1,0,1,2 are

    W=(2/9,2/3,1/3,1/9),                               (12)

and zero elsewhere. Direct substitution verifies the Green equations
with beta/s=(1,3,3,1). For(10), the second differences on these bases are

    Delta^2 f=(c,1-2c,c-1,0).

Thus the exact row identity gives

    sum_j theta_j f_j-f_0
      =(2/9)c+(2/3)(1-2c)+(1/3)(c-1)
      =1/3-7c/9=1/3-7sqrt(5)/27<0.                    (13)

The POSITIVE flux term (2/9)c comes from the empty-residual transit node
at base-1. It is compensated by the negative terms at the next two
bases. No mass was discarded and the original row was not stopped at
first exit or reweighted. This gives a concrete exact cancellation
pattern that the general Green route must account for.

The example refutes automaticity of the sufficient invariant, while
supporting neither a failure of original-row Jensen in this regime nor
a general theorem that its boundary terms always compensate. Its
normalized maximum depth is (22/9)/6=11/27, strictly above OC's2/9.
